source.title: On the Implicit Bias Towards Minimal Depth of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Tomer Galanti; Liane Galanti; Ido Ben-Shaul

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on partially corrupted labels and measures layerwise nearest-class-center separability and classification accuracy, rather than measuring the original claim's fit and test error directly.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on random-label training; those cited results are not rows. Its own experiments vary partial label corruption and report training accuracy and intermediate-layer separability. Figure-only accuracy values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study trains networks with SGD on varying fractions of corrupted labels and reports training and test accuracy, directly testing portions of V4 with the original type of measurement. Its main additional measure, effective NCC depth, does not itself measure any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the reported corruption results. The broader conclusion is that sufficiently deep networks converge to approximately the same effective NCC depth, that this depth increases with label corruption, and that comparing clean-label effective depth with the depth required for partially corrupted labels yields empirically non-vacuous generalization estimates.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SGD with weight decay and measures intermediate-layer nearest-class-center separability and accuracy; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization measurement. It also varies label corruption only partially in its experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, and corruption fraction; effective depth and intermediate-layer separability differ between clean and corrupted-label training.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective NCC depth increases with label corruption: on MNIST it changes from 5 at 0% corruption to 10 at 2% for epsilon 0.01. CIFAR10 also shows reduced intermediate-layer NCC separability with corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random label corruption increases the depth required for training representations to become separable by a nearest-class-center classifier.

record.problems: The main label-corruption accuracy results are presented in plots without exact values; the text describes perfect training fit only for the MNIST CONV-10-50 models with at most 10% corruption. The study does not test completely random labels or report a textual test-error trajectory toward chance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were extracted. Figures 9-12 show further noisy-label plots, but their captions identify some architectures and datasets without giving exact accuracy values in text; the main text already reports the explicit training-fit finding and the central corruption experiment.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, chance test performance, and fitting them with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus completely random labels and convergence slowing across corruption fractions; a fixed 500-epoch budget does not establish these results.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The full corruption range through 100% is not tested. The supplied text does not establish the plotted test-error trend or perfect model training fit across the CIFAR10 corruption conditions.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent fitting completely random labels, and whether removing regularization preserves true-label generalization; no regularization ablation is reported.
Temporal ordering of learning clean patterns and memorizing noise; layerwise separability comparisons do not establish that ordering.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: unreadable plots and untested corruption levels do not demonstrate a failure of V4. Appendix noisy-label experiments are already declared in rows_left_out. Penultimate-layer NCC separability should not be substituted for the trained model's classification accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time or convergence speed across corruption levels.
Shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

A full sweep from no corruption to all labels random; steadily rising test error toward chance; evidence that the model captures remaining signal while memorizing noise. The study reports partial-corruption experiments and layerwise NCC accuracy, with plotted model test accuracy.
Whether regularization methods prevent fitting random labels or whether removing them harms generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.
